Question: What evidence is there for the resurrection?
ShortAnswer: The evidence for the resurrection includes the empty tomb, the eyewitness appearances, the transformation of the disciples, and an early creed dating to within a few years of the event. Together they make the resurrection the best explanation of the facts, not a blind leap.
DetailedAnswer: Start with the earliest evidence: Paul quotes a creed in 1 Corinthians 15:3-7 — 'Christ died for our sins... was buried... was raised on the third day... appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve' — that scholars date to within a few years of the crucifixion, too early for legend to grow. Then the empty tomb: all four Gospels agree the tomb was found empty by women, whose testimony counted for little in that culture — an awkward detail no invented story would include (Mark 16:1-8). Then the appearances: to individuals, to groups, to skeptics like Thomas (John 20:24-29) and James, Jesus' own brother, who had not believed during His ministry (John 7:5) but became a leader of the Jerusalem church. Then the transformation: frightened disciples who fled at Jesus' arrest were, weeks later, publicly proclaiming Him risen in the very city where He was executed (Acts 2:32) — and most would die for that claim. No single piece proves the resurrection alone, but together they point one way: the tomb was empty because Jesus rose. As Paul put it, if Christ has not been raised, Christian faith is useless (1 Corinthians 15:14) — which is exactly why the evidence matters.
